questions.prompt: A hyperbola is the set of points whose distances to the foci (-5, 0) and (5, 0) differ by 6 (in absolute value). Derive its equation.
questions.prompt_markup: A hyperbola is the set of points whose distances to the foci (-5, 0) and (5, 0) differ by 6 (in absolute value). Derive its equation.
questions.required_method: Write the distance difference, isolate one radical, square twice, and simplify.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: |√((x + 5)² + y²) - √((x - 5)² + y²)| = 6; isolate and square; simplify to 5x - 9 = ±3√((x - 5)² + y²) (or equivalent); square again; 16x² - 9y² = 144.
